links.outcome: LLM harmful versus clinically helpful responses in simulated suicide-risk conversations across four risk levels
links.effect: Models varied substantially on severity-weighted mPACT-S score; Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-5.2 scored highest, Grok 4.1 and Mistral Medium 3 lowest; harm avoidance exceeded active helpfulness.
links.quote: Models were generally more successful at avoiding harmful responses than at producing actively helpful ones, and the relationship between harm avoidance and clinically appropriate responding varied across systems.

unlisted_practices: Clinician-authored, risk-stratified (C-SSRS-informed) benchmark with multi-label helpful/less-harmful/more-harmful rating of chatbot responses

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of LLM performance on clinician-authored simulated multi-turn roleplays regarding suicide risk, but tests baseline model responses without testing a specific operational deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
